newsitem.title: FRANCE: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - July 1.
newsitem.headline: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - July 1.

text.p: News from Reuters and the French press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet and Brand-name Products.

PARIS - French health minister Bernard Kouchner says there will be no loosening for next year's soccer World Cup of French laws that ban televising sporting events where billboards show alcohol adverts. But he said promises previously made to Anheuser Busch, a World Cup sponsor and the maker of Budweiser beer, would be taken into account. (Les Echos)

CANNES - Local tastes and cultures are becoming increasingly important for advertisers and their ad agencies, replacing the notion that products can be marketed around the world with a single ad campaign, advertising executives say. (Reuter)

PARIS - France is taking a leading role in opposing moves to ban duty-free shopping within the European Union in 1999. Exports of French-made products, including cosmetics, perfumes and leather goods, would be hit by any such ban. (Le Parisien)

PARIS - French political leaders rebuke Renault SA, the carmaker, for going ahead with plans to close a factory in Belgium, but they also seem eager to turn the page on the embarrassing affair.(Reuter)
PARIS - Pernod Ricard, the French drinks group, has a cautious approach to corporate alliances but Chairman Patrick Ricard says the group remains pragmatic and responsive to the market. (Reuter)

PARIS - The price of shares in LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton are pushed up by the belief in financial circles that the company has carried the first round against British merger partners Guinness Plc and Grand Metropolitan. (Reuter)
